changed_claims.old_text: The board has ten numbered districts in three tiers, five resource tracks in the shared supply, capital/threat/round tracks, and a five-slot turn track. The Root is outside the districts. The resources are energy, consumables, tech, entertainment and credits. Credits in the supply are distinct from players' capital.
changed_claims.new_text: The board has ten numbered districts in three tiers, five resource tracks in the shared supply, capital/threat/round tracks, and a five-slot turn track. The Root is outside the districts. The resources are energy, consumables, tech, entertainment and credits. Credits in the supply are distinct from players' capital. A district's number of colored bars under its name identifies its tier; district borders share the color of their tier. Tiers have no inherent effect on production or threat: particular printed cards may refer to them.
changed_claims.assessment: Verified; no material mismatch or new unsupported rule.

changed_claims.old_text: Except for Melange, a contract triggers only through resolving an action card; it does not matter which player resolves it. Movement out of a district does not count as removal. Returning something to the reserve at the Root does not count as removing it from a district, and triggers no district-removal contract.
changed_claims.new_text: Contract capital always goes to the corporation that owns that contract, regardless of which player resolves the triggering action. Except for Melange, a contract triggers only through resolving an action card; any player may resolve that action. Movement out of a district does not count as removal. Returning something to the reserve at the Root does not count as removing it from a district, and triggers no district-removal contract.
source_refs: RR §§11–11.3,13.1; native corporation sheets both sides
changed_claims.assessment: Verified; no material mismatch or new unsupported rule.

changed_claims.old_text: Placing means taking a component from the reserve. If a newly placed or arriving enemy, illness or outage would duplicate its type in a district, that incoming component moves along the district's exiting arrow toward its higher-numbered destination. Continue through successive destinations until it can stay or reaches the Root. If an enemy is placed/moved into a prisec district, or prisec is placed into a district with enemies, each affected enemy moves; prisec does not remove the enemy. The path exiting Base de Cayambe (10) leads to the Root.
changed_claims.new_text: Placing means taking a component from the reserve. If a newly placed or arriving enemy, illness or outage would duplicate its type in a district, that incoming component moves along the district's exiting arrow toward its higher-numbered destination. Continue through successive destinations until it can stay or reaches the Root. If an enemy is placed/moved into a prisec district, or prisec is placed into a district with enemies, each affected enemy moves; Ordinary prisec protection causes movement rather than a removal effect. The path exiting Base de Cayambe (10) leads to the Root.
changed_claims.assessment: Verified; no material mismatch or new unsupported rule.

changed_claims.old_text: Exploitation and event cards do not trigger illness's action effect. An illness token entering the Root still causes the separate 2-threat Root increase, just like an enemy or outage.
changed_claims.new_text: Exploitation and event cards do not trigger illness's action effect. An illness token entering the Root returns to the reserve and causes the separate 2-threat Root increase, just like an enemy or outage.
changed_claims.assessment: Verified; no material mismatch or new unsupported rule.

changed_claims.old_text: To exhaust an asset, rotate it 90 degrees clockwise. An exhausted asset cannot be exhausted again. Ready your exhausted assets at the start of Refresh, after any start-of-turn triggers. Exhausted assets stay exhausted when traded or stolen. If you control several abilities with the same timing, choose their order. If multiple players use same-timing assets, resolve them clockwise from the active player. Abilities saying “may” and End of Turn abilities are optional; apply the once-per-ability end-of-turn limit in Turn Structure.
changed_claims.new_text: To exhaust an asset, rotate it 90 degrees clockwise. An exhausted asset cannot be exhausted again. Ready your exhausted assets at the start of Refresh, after any start-of-turn triggers, by rotating them 90 degrees counterclockwise to their original orientation. Exhausted assets stay exhausted when traded or stolen. If you control several abilities with the same timing, choose their order. If multiple players use same-timing assets, resolve them clockwise from the active player. Abilities saying “may” and End of Turn abilities are optional; apply the once-per-ability end-of-turn limit in Turn Structure.
changed_claims.assessment: Verified; no material mismatch or new unsupported rule.

changed_claims.old_text: Players cannot tell others which actions are in their hands, and cannot lie about hand counts. Actions stolen or given by an effect remain secret from others. Rivals cannot be revealed or discussed. Do not inspect facedown turn-track assets. Event fronts seen with a look/reorder ability must stay secret; event backs, including the back of the deck's top card, are public.
changed_claims.new_text: Players cannot tell others which actions are in their hands, and cannot lie about hand counts. Actions stolen or given by an effect remain secret from others. Rivals cannot be revealed or discussed during play; all players reveal them when the game ends. Do not inspect facedown turn-track assets. Event fronts seen with a look/reorder ability must stay secret; event backs, including the back of the deck's top card, are public.
changed_claims.assessment: Verified; no material mismatch or new unsupported rule.
